blocks.content: The Government of India Act of 1935 served as a major structural blueprint for the Constitution of Independent India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Regulating Act of 1773 designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal and established a Supreme Court at Calcutta in 1774.
Pitt's India Act of 1784 established a system of double government by separating commercial and political functions of the East India Company.
The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India and centralized legislative powers.
The Government of India Act of 1919 introduced Dyarchy in the provinces and established a bicameral legislature at the Centre.
The Government of India Act of 1935 proposed an All-India Federation, introduced Provincial Autonomy, and served as the primary structural blueprint for the Indian Constitution.

rows: Abolished Dyarchy in Provinces; Introduced Provincial Autonomy
Proposed All-India Federation & Dyarchy at the Centre
Limited franchise based on property, tax, or education
Extended franchise to about 10% of the total population

items: Dyarchy was introduced at the Provincial level by the GOI Act 1919 and shifted to the Centre by the GOI Act 1935.
The Supreme Court at Calcutta was established under the Regulating Act of 1773 (in 1774) with Sir Elijah Impey as Chief Justice.
The division of powers into Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent lists was first introduced under the Government of India Act 1935.
